author: Ash

copy.intro: You've picked a Scuffers hoodie, switched the store to the US and watched €79 turn into $109. That price does cover import taxes, but free shipping starts at $400 and you get 14 days to send it back. So here are 12 brands making the same kind of hoodie that ship to the US, from Madrid neighbors to American labels. The ones closest to Scuffers' $109 to $119 come first.

bodies.gramicci:
Gramicci is the closest match on price: every full-price hoodie it sells is $115, right between Scuffers' $109 pullovers and $119 zip-ups. The GCE Hooded Sweatshirt ($115) is the one to start with, in an 87% cotton fleeceback blend.

It's a climbing brand first. It started in 1982 in a garage in Ventura, California, making climbing shorts, and the hoodies sit alongside its G-Pants. Free shipping starts at $175, far below Scuffers' $400. Returns are open for 30 days, though a US return costs $9 for the label and exchanges are free.

The catch is choice, because only a handful of hoodies are at full price at any time. If you want a deep range for the same money, Dormers Club has far more.
bodies.yujin-clothing:
Yujin Clothing is the pick if you want to spend a little less and need bigger sizes. Most of its hoodies cost $78 or $82, and many go up to 5XL, three sizes past Scuffers' XXL. The YUJIN Essential Otaku Hoodie ($70) is the simple one to start with.

It's a Japanese anime streetwear label, so the artwork is anime-led. Prices rise a few dollars on the biggest sizes, and the tie-dye hoodies jump to $158 to $160.

Two things to know before you order. Its own listings say the hoodies run small and suggest going one size up. And everything is made to order, so a wrong size can't be returned or exchanged. Check the size chart twice, or go to Blanks by Thirteen, which takes returns for 30 days.
bodies.berlinc:
Berlinc is where to go for a heavier hoodie at Scuffers' price. Scuffers calls its Raw hoodies midweight, while Berlinc cuts everything from 500 gsm cotton fleece. The V2 Monochrome Sunfaded Hoodie ($120), a remake of its best seller, has a sun-faded wash, and the Heather Gray Hoodie ($95) gives you the same weight for less.

It's a small Californian label that makes in small batches. Newer pieces are sometimes sold as pre-orders, which take six to eight weeks, but in-stock hoodies ship the next business day. US orders ship free over $200.

The catch is returns. There are no refunds, only size exchanges within 7 days. If you want room to change your mind, Gramicci and Blanks by Thirteen both give you 30 days.
bodies.dormers-club:
Dormers Club, which spells itself DRMERS CLUB, gives you the most hoodies to choose from at Scuffers' price. Most cost $110, like the Arch Hoodie, while the Signature Basic Hoodie ($100) is the plain one and the Pin Hoodie ($125) is the novelty.

It's a Vancouver label with one store, in Gastown. US orders take 6 to 12 business days and cost $7 to ship, or nothing over $150. Sizes run from XS to XXXL, one past Scuffers.

Returns are 14 days, the same as Scuffers, and you pay the postage. But limited drops and collaborations can't go back at all, so check which kind you're buying.
bodies.blue-banana:
Blue Banana is the other Madrid brand that's closest on price, and its Classic hoodie (€94.90, about $106) comes in just under Scuffers' $109. It's 100% organic cotton in a regular fit, with the brand's X embroidered on the chest and back.

The thing to know is the currency. Blue Banana charges US shoppers in euros, and €94.90 is its US price. The same hoodie is €69.90 in Spain.

Shipping to the US costs €5.90, or nothing over €125. But customs charges are yours, while Scuffers pays them for you. Returns are open for 30 days, twice Scuffers' window, though exchanges are only for Spain and Portugal.
bodies.von-dutch:
Von Dutch covers both ends of Scuffers' price. The Remi Waffle Hoodie ($65) and the Velour Zip Up ($65) cost far less, while the Spider Crest Hoodie ($130) sits a little above.

It's the trucker-cap brand of the early 2000s, now owned by White Space Group, and the hoodies run from velour zips to spider-logo pullovers. Sizes go from XS to 2XL, though some styles stop at XL.

The catch is returns. Von Dutch takes none, only exchanges, and you buy the return label yourself. If you might change your mind, Nude Project gives you 30 days.
bodies.nude-project:
Nude Project is the closest thing to Scuffers' own story: a Spanish label started in 2018 by two friends, with hoodies at similar money. The Origins Hoodie ($99) starts below Scuffers, and most sit at $129 or $139, like the Biggie Hoodie ($129).

It has a store in New York, at 42 Greene Street, so you can try a size on before ordering. Online, US prices include taxes and duties, shipping is free over $400 like at Scuffers, and returns run 30 days, double Scuffers' 14.

The Origins Hoodie is a regular fit in 400 g brushed fleece, so it sits closer than the boxy styles. On the zip-ups, the brand suggests sizing down for a closer fit.
bodies.wesc:
WeSC is the simple way to spend less. Every full-price hoodie is $88, about $20 under Scuffers, and the Dropped Shoulder Hoodie in the Enzyme Wash Palm Logo print ($88) is the one to look at, with an oversized cut.

It was founded in Stockholm in 1999 around skateboarding and music, and today it ships from a Los Angeles warehouse. Orders over $150 ship free.

The range is small, and these hoodies are a lightweight loopback summer fleece rather than a heavy winter one. Returns are 14 days, like Scuffers, and you pay the postage. For a heavier hoodie under $90, Blanks by Thirteen is the better bet.
bodies.blanks-by-thirteen:
Blanks by Thirteen is the cheapest route to a heavy, plain hoodie made in the USA. The Perfect Hoodie ($78) is 450 GSM combed cotton fleece milled in California, and the washed versions, like the Faded Black Hoodie, are $85.

It's a blank-apparel company, so you're paying for the hoodie rather than a graphic. The fit is slightly oversized with dropped shoulders, close to Scuffers' oversized cut, and the brand suggests sizing down for a true fit.

US orders ship free over $100, and returns are open for 30 days. Its Blanks Limited drops don't restock, so a color you like may not come back.
bodies.mod-wave-movement:
Mod Wave Movement is the Madrid pick for something louder, and it costs more, with US prices from $182 to $330. The Sudadera con capucha oversized ($194) is the plainest way in, and the studded Vanguard Dogs hoodie ($330) is the statement piece.

The brand describes itself as dark fashion with Asian aesthetics, and genderless, which puts it a long way from Scuffers' everyday hoodies. Sizes start at XXS, handy if Scuffers' XS is too big.

Shipping to the US starts at €30, duties aren't included, and returns are 14 days. If you want graphic hoodies for far less, Yujin Clothing's anime designs mostly cost $78 to $82.
bodies.akimbo-club:
Akimbo Club is the step up in weight, and in price. Its plain Hoodie ($160) is 14 oz brushed cotton in a relaxed, boxy fit, the Zip-Up Hoodie is $170, and the Watch-Peeker zip-ups reach $250.

It's a Utah brand that ships from its own fulfillment center there, with US orders going by USPS Priority Mail. Alongside its own line it sells some vintage pieces, so check the listing if you want the Akimbo label.

The catch is big: US sales are final, with no returns or exchanges. Know your size first, or start with Berlinc's 500 gsm hoodies at $95 to $145, which at least allow a size exchange.
bodies.picante:
Picante is the luxury option, a London brand whose Everyday Hoodie costs $270 in the US. It's a boxy, slightly cropped fit in heavy organic brushed-back cotton, garment dyed and hand-sprayed so each one comes out a little different.

The US price sits well above the UK one (£145), but it includes all taxes and duties, and US orders over $300 ship free. Returns are open for 14 days, at your cost.

Higher up, the Faux Fur Lined Sun-Faded Zip-Up Hoodie is $720. If you want a sun-faded wash for a fraction of that, Berlinc's V2 Monochrome Sunfaded Hoodie is $120.

closing.heading: How to choose
closing.body:
Start with what you want to spend. Gramicci and Berlinc sit right around Scuffers' $109 to $119, and so does most of Dormers Club. Under $90, Blanks by Thirteen is the heavy plain hoodie and WeSC is the lighter one.

Then think about what happens if it doesn't fit. Nude Project, Blue Banana and Blanks by Thirteen give you 30 days. Akimbo Club and Von Dutch take no returns, and Yujin Clothing won't take back a wrong size, so measure first there.

And if you don't want a bill at the door, Nude Project and Picante include US duties, as Scuffers does. Blue Banana and Mod Wave Movement leave customs to you.

faqs.a: In Madrid, Spain. Jaime Cruz and Javier López founded it there in 2018, and its stores are in Madrid, Barcelona and Valencia.

faqs.q: How long does Scuffers take to ship to the US?
faqs.a: Standard US delivery takes 2 to 5 days and costs $10, or nothing on orders over $400. Scuffers covers the import taxes, so there's nothing extra to pay on delivery.
faqs.source_query: how long does scuffers take to ship to the us

faqs.a: Yes, in Spain: Madrid, Barcelona and Valencia. It has run pop-ups in London, Amsterdam and Los Angeles, but there's no permanent US store, so US shoppers buy online.
In the US, $109 for a pullover and $119 for a zip-up, import taxes included. In Spain the same hoodies cost €79 and €82, which converts to about $88 and $91.
